PARIS — Advanced Acoustic Concepts, a US defense subsidiary of the global defense giant Thales Group , has secured a $53.9 million contract with the US Navy to deliver at least two remote mine hunting (RMH) modules aimed at bolstering sailor safety when tracking mines.
“The ability to counter undersea mine threats remains fundamental to maritime security and naval mission success,” Rob Geckle, CEO of Thales North America, said in a statement Monday. “By advancing the Navy’s [mine countermeasures] capabilities, this program will help strengthen fleet readiness and support mission success in an increasingly dynamic operating environment.”
The contract comes as mine countermeasure operations have taken the spotlight amid operations in the Middle East like Operation Epic Fury , where US Central Command kicked off mine clearing missions in the Strait of Hormuz in April. President Donald Trump said in August mines in the waterway were cleared.
The contract also covers engineering support for the modules, and has the possibility to climb to $196.2 million for subsequent modules. The first two modules are slated for delivery by October 2029, with potential follow-on modules delivered through 2039 and beyond.
The RMH features Thales’ SAMDIS 600 sonar that can provide high-resolution imaging of potential mines, along with an AI software so sailors can analyze the data quickly and accurately, according to Thales. The SAMDIS 600 sonar was recently tested with an unmanned underwater vehicle from HII for a mine countermeasures exercise .
Tony Lengerich, vice president of naval programs with Thales Defense & Security, Inc., told Breaking Defense that Thales’ SAMDIS 600 sonar features a three-beam system that allows a “highly improved probability of certainty” during one sweep through a minefield.
“You get three looks at an object instead of just one look,” Lengerich said. “Those three pictures, if you will, really increase the certainty that you’re looking at a mine, not a Volkswagen somebody tossed in the ocean somewhere. So, speed of detection, speed of certainty, is now what we’re improving.”
Relatedly, Thales and HII announced today they recently teamed up to deploy Thales’ SAMDIS 600 sonar on HII’s Remus 620 UUV , which is capable of conducting long-range, multi-day operations.
Together, they used Thales’ Expeditionary Portable Operation Center command and control system to function as the “operational hub,” along with HII’s command and control software known as Odyssey to facilitate mission planning and management to scout potential mine threats, the firms said in a joint news release today.
“They can program that thing to go through the minefield surface, send back the data, and continue to keep searching,” Lengerich said.
Additionally, the exercise also employed HII’s automated launch and recovery system called Sea Launcher to deploy and retrieve the REMUS vehicle underwater. The launcher system can be paired with either manned or unmanned systems, further removing sailors from the minefield, according to HII.
“Keeping the sailor out of the field is a critical part of that,” Nicholas Green, senior manager of international business development with HII, told Breaking Defense. “But another part is actually getting the equipment in and out of the water. That’s always been a difficult part of what we do. And the Sea Launcher is the latest iteration of what we are offering for launch and recovery of our medium sized UUV.”
After analyzing the data collected from the sonar and UUV, the teams deployed Thales’ Advanced Acoustic Concepts’ ANGLER underwater effector to neutralize detected mines.

2026 Chevrolet Trailblazer Gets Three "Poor" Ratings From the IIHS
19 photos
Photo: IIHS on YouTube / edited
In the updated moderate overlap frontal crash test, Chevy's Trailblazer could not do better than "poor" by IIHS standards. Per the nonprofit organization, the rear dummy chest protection was rated "marginal." The bad news continues with "poor" ratings for rear dummy kinematics and restraints, and that's especially interesting because GM apparently changed the rear seatbelt load limiters on 2026 models produced after February 2026.
General Motors made those changes to improve rear occupant protection in this exact crash scenario, but alas, it was not enough. On the upside, the rear dummy's head misses the front seatback. The Trailblazer does a much better job up front, with the driver scoring "good" for thigh, hip, lower leg, foot, chest, neck, and head protection in the moderate overlap crash test.
GM also revised the Trailblazer 's side structure and thorax side airbag, all in the name of improving occupant safety in side impact crashes. Compared to the moderate overlap test, the small crossover earned a "good" rating in this evaluation. The small overlap frontal test also ended with a "good" rating.
As far as headlight performance is concerned, both the LS and LT get "acceptable" ratings for their front lights due to some glare. RS and Activ grades also use LED projectors, yet their headlights were deemed "poor" due to excessive low-beam glare and visibility issues for the high beams on the left side of straight roads and through the sharp right-hand curve.
Photo: IIHS on YouTube The standard automatic emergency braking system of the Trailblazer is "poor" across the board in vehicle-against-vehicle scenarios, but curiously enough, the IIHS deemed it "marginal" in situations that involve pedestrians. For example, the system avoided a collision with a crossing child at 12 miles per hour and cut impact speed by 22 in the 25-mph scenario.
Based on the VSS-F platform, the Chevy-branded twin of the Buick Encore GX hails from the Bupyeong plant in South Korea. Previously made in China as well, the Trailblazer was refreshed in October 2026 for the 2027 model year . The redesigned Trailblazer is due to hit dealer showrooms next spring with numerous changes, including a standard 1.3-liter turbo I3.
Previously, a 1.2 served as the base engine. Its trims have been reduced from four to three, namely the base Trailblazer, the sporty-looking RS, and the off-road Z71 instead of the Activ grade. Chevrolet waxes lyrical about more than 20 standard safety and driver-assistance features, including reverse automatic braking, rear cross-traffic braking, and intersection automatic emergency braking.
For the time being, the 2026 model has to suffice. Prices kick off at $25,395 for the LS with the 1.2-liter engine or $26,990 with the larger mill. All-wheel drive will set you back $27,395 at the very least. LS ships with 11-inch touchscreen infotainment, an 8-inch driver information center screen, 17-inch alloys, a fold-flat front passenger seat, and an HD rear vision camera.
The LT levels up to nicer wheels, keyless open and start, remote start, deep-tinted rear windows and liftgate glass, and silver on the roof rails. The Activ and RS both ship with the 1.3-liter engine by default, with both starting at $28,200 as of this writing. Naturally, the priciest grades available for 2026 also come with the most desirable and usable of standard goodies.

Q&A: Fresh Electric Dirt Bike Player, Yozma, Is Attending EICMA With New IN11 – Here's What's Coming
14 photos
Photo: Cristian Curmei | Autoevolution
Ever since Yozma appeared on the scene back in 2025, they quickly swept across the US with their fun and capable electric mini dirt bikes. Well, they’re attending EICMA for the first time, and also showcasing their latest IN11 and 11 Pro, so, we decided to get in touch with the brand for a quick Q&A to see what’s in store here and where they’re headed.
If the name Yozma isn’t familiar to you, once you're done with this quick Q&A, your social media feed is sure to toss some ads at you. But, what you do need to know about Yozma is that they’re a rather new kid on the block, and instead of positing themselves against others like Sur-Ron, Talaria, and a few consecrated e-dirt bike brands, Yozma chose to supply a different segment of the market: off-road-loving mini dirt bikes.
Photo: Cristian Curmei | Autoevolution Building on the success of the IN10 and 10 Pro series bikes that carry a customer review rating of a minimum of 4.8 out of 5 stars, Yozma has decided to step up their lineup with the similar level of off-road-ready rides, but ones that can now carry out some stunts. Let’s see what Yozma has to say about the new series.
Our first question for the brand is one that reveals a bit about what the IN11 and 11 Pro lineup has in store for interested riders, and while it may an answer that is marketing-oriented, it does give us an idea of what gap the IN11 fills in Yozma’s lineup.
Autoevolution (AE) : For new riders just discovering Yozma, how would you define your brand's DNA and what was the vision behind creating both the IN11 and IN11 Pro series?
Yozma : " At Yozma, our DNA is 100% pure off-road excitement. We build strictly off-road electric dirt bikes designed for maximum control, instant torque, and pure riding fun without emissions. With the IN11 Series, we wanted to cater to different riding styles and skill levels.
The IN11 is our agile, playful, and stunt-ready bike—perfect for riders looking for dynamic fun, agility, and clever features like Auto-Wheelie Assist.
On the other hand, the IN11 PRO is built for extreme performance, higher power output, and riders who want to push boundaries on tough, challenging trails. "
Do take not of the fact that the 11 Pro does have a range of 85 km (53 miles) and a peak torque output of 245 Nm (181 lb-ft), so 45 Nm (33 lb-ft) more than the standard IN11.
Photo: Cristian Curmei | Autoevolution AE : How does the IN11 PRO step up performance for off-road enthusiasts?
Yozma : " The IN11 PRO - while it retains that core spirit of the standard IN11 and the Wheelie Assist and built-in Anti-Tip Protection - is engineered for riders looking for higher-tier performance and more aggressive off-road capability. Both models share our high standards for safety and agility, but the IN11 Pro is all about unlocking smart, stunt-ready fun . "
Simply put, Yozma is now chasing the stunt dragon that countless other brands on the market are now setting their sights on, but still reserves its off-road spirit with knobby tires, a plush suspension, and more kick than the standard models this brand has brought to market until now. Be sure to check out our previous coverage on the Yozma lineup to catch up if you’re not aware of who they are and what this crew brings to the table.
Photo: Cristian Curmei | Autoevolution AE : EICMA is the world’s biggest platform for two-wheelers. How do you see electric dirt bikes changing the off-road market, and what is Yozma’s roadmap for Europe and global markets moving forward?
Yozma : " The off-road sector is undergoing a massive transformation. Electric dirt bikes aren't just about zero emissions—they offer instant torque without gear shifting, minimal noise, which opens up more places to ride without disturbing nature or local communities, and dramatically lower maintenance costs.”
“EICMA 2026 is a major milestone for Yozma as we expand into European and international markets. We are establishing direct connections with local distributors, dealers, and the off-road community and are fully committed to building a strong global service network, supporting riders with reliable performance and continuously elevating the electric off-road experience. "
Photo: Cristian Curmei | Autoevolution Yes, Yozma is growing and setting its sights on one very important aspect of customer relations: the network of dealers and distributors, meaning that if we do need parts and servicing, we won’t need to stand by for weeks to months to be back on our ride, and if I may, I already tested Yozma’s ability to quickly meet our needs.
I’m currently testing an IN10 Pro and I initially thought I had an issue with the battery – I don’t, but Yozma felt we shouldn’t risk anything, even though the pack seems to be working within parameters – it's currently mounted in the 10 Pro. So, they decided to send a new one over, and if I may, within a week, the new pack was in my hands. Simply put, they already have distribution centers and parts replacement for my area.
Since we’re here at EICMA, we’ve also put together a video interview for Yozma and will be including it in some coverage that we run on the event. Keep your eyes peeled for content on our social media channels if you don’t feel like reading EICMA coverage.

New Matchbox Collector Series Cars for 2027: Is It Time to Lose Hope?
24 photos
Photo: Lamley Group
For the first time in weeks, one of my local toy stores just brought in a new case of Hot Wheels Mainline models. I wasn’t exactly sure which one it was though, as I couldn’t recall where the green Mazda RX-7, silver Audi R8 Convertible and blue Ferrari 12Cilindri belonged.
I found the answer the moment I spotted the black Nissan Skyline HT 2000GT-X, which was the official Treasure Hunt collectible for this year’s Case P. Yes, that’s how far behind we are right now. I just showed you a preview of 2027’s Case C about a week ago, and the stores here aren’t even done with 2026 yet. I also spoke to one of my dealers to keep an old Impala safe for me until he brings in more cars.
It’s an item I don’t even remember seeing before, and you’ll be shocked by the size of the wheels. Now, I’m debating whether I should order 10 more Matchbox Moving Parts models from a buddy of mine I haven’t worked with in a while.
He’s the only person who has them in stock in a 300-mile radius, and I’ve often loved unboxing cars from that series. I can’t say the same thing about the Collector Series though, which seems stuck in a loop that it may never get out of.
Sure, they all have True Grip tires, but the wheels are often disappointing. And that’s not the worst part. I realize having moving parts on all of them might jeopardize Mattel’s Hot Wheels Premium lines. But having us guess all the time which models are “sealed” and which aren’t has become tedious. Now, Mr. Lambert seems to think this case will be the only one we’ll get in 2027, just because of the numbering system.
Photo: Lamley Group Matchbox usually used x/20 as opposed to what you’ll see in Car Culture (1/5). I think it’s highly improbable that the die cast manufacturer is planning to retire this series: this is change is probably meant to avoid any confusion for the future. You’ll spot six items inside, and there’s no new casting this time. The 1990 Corvette ZR1 debuted earlier this year (#8 of 20) with a simple red finish and gray 5-spoke wheels.
Seeing it in yellow with a few decals should make it more enticing, but I can’t stand black wheels and the stance seems off, too. I’m not saying I’ll 100% ignore it if I find one in the wild, but it’s not my favorite model in this case.
The 2007 Land Rover 6x6 is available both as a basic release and a Moving Parts collectible. It should have an opening hood which is a bonus. Chances are it will be the first one to fly off the pegs, as we don’t have that many 6x6 options to choose from anyway.
Item #3 of 6 for the mix is the 1988 Porsche 911 Turbo Slant Nose which looked fairly promising in black. It has had a metal base since day one, and I confess I’m surprised to see the Promotional Toy Show Leipzig variation in this video as Mattel only made 250 of them.
Photo: Lamley Group The new color combo looks dull at best, although I suspect it could be derived from a real-world livery. The 1993 Jaguar XJ220s first showed up in 2025, and I was almost convinced I’d get one.
It all changed when I saw it live, and I’ve ignored it twice so far. Third time’s a charm, right? This light blue isn’t the first color that comes to mind when thinking about the British supercar, which isn’t to say it doesn’t look look brilliant on it.
I almost don’t mind the wheels either. Having the 1984 Audi Quattro Sport S1 in here is slightly strange, given it was inside the same case with the Jaguar this year as well.
It’s sporting a different livery this time, and I might buy it just so I can do a close-up comparison with the one from Tarmac Works . The Datsun 240Z Rally is #4 of 6 for the set, and this is its second iteration so far.
Photo: Lamley Group To me, that’s further evidence that Mattel won’t pull the plug on the series just yet, as it wouldn’t be a financially-wise decision considering the licensing costs involved. Is it time to lose hope in this series?
I would think not, especially since it has delivered quite a few collectibles over the past few years. Think back at 2022’s 1963 Honda T360, 1935 Ford Pickup and 1964 Chevy C10 Longbed. One year later Mattel revealed the 1979 Freightliner FLT (which never got a second chance) and the 1953 Ford COE (which I unboxed a variation of last year).
Things seemed to have started to go downhill in 2024, but I can assure you 2025’s 1978 Ford Bronco is a real hit! I’ll give you a taste of a special Autozam soon!

GXO Logistics reported third-quarter revenue of $3.59 billion, a 5.7% increase from a year earlier, as the global contract logistics provider secured more new business and expanded its sales pipeline to record levels.
The Greenwich, Connecticut-based company (NYSE: GXO ) said Tuesday that organic revenue grew 6.4% during the quarter ended Sept. 30, its fastest pace in more than three years.
GXO also reported $375 million in new business wins, a 34% year-over-year increase and the second consecutive quarter in which new contract wins grew more than 30%.
The company’s sales pipeline reached a record $3.1 billion, up more than 30% from a year earlier, signaling continued demand for outsourced warehousing, distribution and supply chain services.
“The new strategy we put in motion over the past year is delivering results,” GXO CEO Patrick Kelleher said in a news release .
Kelleher said the company is winning more business across its core markets and strategic growth sectors while improving its ability to convert opportunities into revenue.
GXO Q3 financial performance
GXO reported net income of $65 million, compared with $60 million during the same period in 2025. Diluted earnings per share increased to 56 cents from 51 cents.
Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) remained unchanged at $251 million, while adjusted diluted earnings per share rose to 89 cents from 79 cents.
However, operating income declined to $96 million from $118 million, and adjusted EBITDA margin narrowed to 7% from 7.4%.
The company also reported a decline in operating cash flow to $156 million from $232 million a year earlier. Free cash flow fell to $85 million from $187 million.
Direct operating expenses increased to $3.06 billion from $2.86 billion, outpacing revenue growth and contributing to pressure on operating profitability.

Source: GXO Logistics Q3 2026 earnings release, financial statements and non-GAAP reconciliations. Percentage-point changes are labeled pp. Organic revenue growth for Q3 2025 was not separately provided in the release.
New contracts drive growth across strategic industries
GXO said its year-to-date new business wins exceeded $1 billion, nearly matching the company’s total contract wins for all of 2025 with one quarter remaining.
Around 40% of those wins came from strategic growth industries, including aerospace and defense, technology, industrial operations and life sciences.
The company’s technology and consumer electronics business generated $498 million in third-quarter revenue, up 18.6% from $420 million a year earlier.
Industrial and manufacturing revenue increased 4.9% to $405 million, while omnichannel retail, GXO’s largest customer segment, generated $1.69 billion, up 2.7%.
Food and beverage revenue declined 5.4% to $351 million.
The United Kingdom remained GXO’s largest geographic market, generating $1.75 billion in quarterly revenue, an increase of 7.6%.
U.S. revenue rose 5.6% to $846 million, compared with $801 million during the third quarter of 2025.
GXO reaffirms 2026 financial outlook
Despite lower operating margins and cash flow during the quarter, GXO reaffirmed its full-year 2026 financial guidance.
The company continues to project:
Organic revenue growth of 4% to 5%.
Adjusted EBITDA of $945 million to $965 million.
Adjusted diluted earnings per share of $2.95 to $3.15.
Free cash flow conversion of 30% to 40%.
Through the first nine months of 2026, GXO generated $10.33 billion in revenue, up 6.8% from $9.67 billion during the same period last year.
Nine-month adjusted EBITDA totaled $670 million, compared with $626 million a year earlier.
GXO also repurchased $84 million in common stock during the third quarter, bringing year-to-date share repurchases to $100 million.
As of Sept. 30, the company reported $340 million in cash and cash equivalents and approximately $2.8 billion in outstanding debt.
GXO will hold its third-quarter earnings conference call at 8:30 a.m. Wednesday.
Why it matters: GXO’s accelerating contract wins and record sales pipeline indicate strengthening demand for outsourced logistics services, although declining operating margins and free cash flow highlight the challenge of converting revenue growth into higher profitability.

2026 SEMA Show • 2027 Toyota Crown Signia Gets GT-S Concept Treatment for SEMA, Becomes a Sleek Wagon
Someone Paid $2.3 Million for a Ferrari Daytona SP3, Drove 80 Miles, Sold for $18.5 Million
29 photos
Photo: Broad Arrow Auctions
A Ferrari Daytona SP3 just sold for a mind-blowing $18,540,000 just two years after its original owner had paid $2.3 million to drive it off the showroom floor. He obviously bought it as an investment, hoping to cash in one day, but what it returned must have surpassed his expectations by far.
When Ferrari launched the Daytona SP3 , it carried a base sticker price of $2,250,000 in the United States. For this specific example, the original owner paid $2,334,048. So how in the world did it end up as a 794% return on investment in just two years?
Finished in the show-stopping Verde Franesca, chassis number 314846, was originally ordered through Ferrari North America in Englewood, New Jersey, and delivered directly to the owner via Ferrari of Long Island, which means the first owner must have been based somewhere in the New York metropolitan area.
The green Ferrari Daytona SP3's official paperwork and special-series "Yellow Book" record its build completion date as October 2024, which means it must have been delivered either in late 2024 or early 2025. The car was sold exactly two years after it rolled off the production line in Maranello, Italy.
Photo: Broad Arrow Auctions At the second annual Broad Arrow Auctions Las Vegas Sale, which took place at the luxury Wynn Las Vegas resort, the Daytona sold for a $18,540,000 gross sale price, including the buyer's premium, after the hammer dropped at exactly $16,850,000, setting the ultimate world record price for a non-charity production example of the Ferrari Daytona SP3.
In Vegas, bidding escalated quickly in million-dollar offers with two primary bidders being at the forefront of the battle, who advanced from $25,000 to $25,000, holding their ground avidly as the auction crept all the way to $15,850,000. Reports from the scene reveal a controversial moment, with an underbidder claiming their last-second bid was missed.
With the room going crazy, the auctioneer made the exceptionally rare, high-stakes decision to cancel the hammer price and reopen bidding at $16,660,000. The bidders pushed the price up another quarter-million dollars, and the car was definitely hammered at $16,850,000.
So what is special about the world’s second most expensive Ferrari SP3 Daytona? Unlike most owners who prefer to order their Ferraris in Rosso Corsa, Rosso Magma , which was also the launch color for the model, Giallo Modena, or Nero Daytona, this one is finished in the ultra-rare Verde Franesca.
Photo: Broad Arrow Auctions It is a light metallic sage green selected through the Tailor Made program and acquired for a $42,185 premium, which is basically BMW X1 or Mercedes-Benz GLA money. The car sports a glossy removable carbon fiber targa hardtop, matching the lower bodywork trims, front splitter, side sills, and the rear decklid. Custom airbrushed Scuderia Ferrari shields show up on the fenders.
It rides on the factory five-spoke forged lightweight alloy wheels, hiding the gloss-black brake calipers, with Pirelli P Zero Corsa high-performance tires. The cabin takes exclusivity one step further, with an incredibly unique two-tone combination of Nero Alcantara and Mustard Aunde Jeans denim fabric.
At the moment of the auction, the one-owner Ferrari Daytona SP3 supercar came out of an elite private collection as what was basically a brand-new model, with the odometer displaying only 81 miles (130 kilometers).
This means that the owner didn't really enjoy what the mid-rear, transversely mounted 6.5-liter V12 with naturally aspirated firepower can do. Redlining at 9,500 rpm, the V12 pushes out 829 horsepower (840 metric horsepower) and 514 pound-feet (697 Newton meters) of torque.
Photo: Broad Arrow Auctions That is enough to make it flash from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 2.75 seconds, hit 124 mph (200 kph) in 7.4 seconds, and max out at over 211 mph (340 kph). At launch, it was the most powerful un-electrified, pure internal combustion road engine that Ferrari had ever engineered. A seven-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission puts the power down through the rear wheel.
For over $18 million, the buyer is going home with the Yellow Book, Ferrari’s special-series certification, matching custom red leather luggage, driving gloves, and a highly detailed 1:8 scale Amalgam model, precisely mimicking the car’s silhouette with the swept panoramic windshield, dramatic butterfly doors, and prominent rear horizontal slats.
Ferrari is building only 599+1 Daytona SP3s, which makes the model exceptionally rare. That is probably why the price on the used car market has gone through the roof. Just under three months prior to the Las Vegas Auction, a yellow Ferrari Daytona SP3 sold for $17,825,000 at RM Sotheby's Monterey Car Week back in August.
The only SP3 to ever command more than the one finished in Verde Franesca was a one-off two-tone example finished in Giallo Modena (what did I tell you about paint colors?) and exposed carbon fiber that sold for $26,000,000 at RM Sotheby's Monterey Car Week last year. However, that was a pure charity example built specifically to benefit the Ferrari Foundation.

Grandson Is Selling the Cadillac His Grandpa Bought New Back in 1958
23 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer
This 1958 Cadillac Series 62 Sedan has spent 68 years with the same family. Now, the grandson of the original owner has decided to pass it on to someone who has the time and the motivation to pamper it for the rest of its life. And considering it has been treated like a member of the family so far, it looks like it has plenty of life left in it.
The grandfather of the current owner walked into the Bayer Cadillac dealership in New York one day back in 1958 and drove off in this Cadillac Series 62 Sedan. Finished in black and white over a black and white interior, the car looks like pure Americana royalty.
It rides on 15-inch steel wheels with bright covers and Remington Cushion-Aire whitewall tires, and yes, they are the wheels on which the car drove off the showroom floor. The 1958 Cadillac Series 62 Sedan stands at the height of late 1950s American extravaganza, showing off the massive scale, jet-age styling, and heavy chrome ornamentation, all under the guidance of design guru Harley Earl.
It comes with the egg-crate, wide and heavy-texture grille, sitting above a front bumper that integrates the prominent bullet-style guards, the so-called Dagmars. The 1958 model year marked the transition to dual-headlight setups integrated into the front fenders.
Photo: Bring a Trailer The four-window sedan, just like its six-window sibling, features a pillarless hardtop profile, which, with all the windows rolled down, displays an uninterrupted opening to the cabin. The layout also simplified entry and exit.
The rear end was just as impressive as the front, sporting high-mounted, sharply angled tailfins, with their presence confirming the model's signature jet-age silhouette. Dual bullet-style taillights anchor the tips of the fins.
Imposing stance, indimidating appearance From the Dagmars to those fins, the car, which is a short-deck model, stretches 216.8 inches (5,507 millimeters) in length. It measured 80.0 inches (2,032 millimeters) in width and 59.1 inches (1,501 millimeters) in height, sitting on a wheelbase of 129.5 inches (3,289 millimeters).
The sedan, underpinned by General Motors’ C-body architecture with Fisher body construction, tips the scales at 4,675 pounds (2,121 kilograms). That is how much the V8 from under the hood has to pull. It is a 365-cubic-inch (6.0-liter) power plant with a four-barrel carburetor. The setup produces 310 horsepower (314 metric horsepower) and 405 pound-feet (459 Newton meters) of torque for a top speed of 120 mph (193 kph).
Photo: Bring a Trailer General Motors also offered the optional Eldorado 365-cubic-inch V8 at the time, bringing 335 horsepower (340 metric horsepower) but less torque (400 pound-feet/542 Newton meters) for a top speed slightly increased to 123 mph (198 kph).
A four-speed Hydra-Matic automatic transmission puts the power down through the rear wheels. Power steering, power windows, and automatic headlight dimmers are also on the menu, while drums at each corner provide the stopping power.
The standard 365 cubic-inch V8 was renowned for being an exceptionally smooth, quiet, and refined engine, matching the comfort offered by the cabin wrapped in plush materials such as Venetian and Victoria cloths and heavy metallic accents.
A luxury lounge on wheels The generous onboard space, provided by the equally generous wheelbase, offered deep, sofa-like front and rear bench seating with fold-down center armrests, giving the occupants the feeling that they were traveling in a mobile luxury lounge. That mobile luxury lounge is fitted with white and black vinyl in this Caddy, which also comes with a push-button AM radio, an analog clock, and a heater.
Photo: Bring a Trailer The two-spoke steering wheel with a chrome horn ring frames a speedometer scaled up to 120 mph, sitting alongside gauges that indicate the coolant temperature and fuel level. The five-digit odometer shows this luxury sedan has traveled 49,413 miles (79,523 kilometers).
Expectedly, the 68-year-old Cadillac is far from perfect. The seller reports an oil leak and seepage from two freeze plugs. The windshield wipers have given their last breath along the way. But everything except the tires is original and incredibly well maintained, which speaks volumes about how it has been taken care of over the years.
This is what the grandson of the original owner is selling right now. The 1958 Cadillac Series 62 comes with a Massachusetts title in the owner’s name. Listed on Bring a Trailer, it definitely stole the show on the platform, as many rushed into the comments section to sing its praises.
However, there is no bidding war. At least not yet. With five days to go, the highest bid hit $3,600. Back in 1958, the Series 62 Sedan with the 365-cubic-inch V8 started at $4,891. Adjusted for inflation, that would be roughly $53,300 today.
Photo: Bring a Trailer Nowadays, such cars sell for anything between $15,000 and $40,000, depending on originality, condition, and mileage . Show-quality cars, frame-off restorations, or incredibly low-mileage original survivors typically go beyond the $100,000 mark.

This Tuned 2027 BMW 3 Series Neue Klasse Lives in Fantasy Land, Do You Like the CGI Makeover?
10 photos
Photo: Instagram | ildar_project
It may feel like it’s been a while since the new-generation BMW 3 Series premiered, but it hasn’t, because this model is less than two months old.
The unveiling took place at the end of September 2026, and it will also touch down in the United States of America to absolutely no one’s surprise, though you will have to wait a bit for that to happen, because the order book will open in the first quarter of 2027. The official website shows that customers will have to choose between the 330 Sedan, 330 xDrive Sedan, and M350 xDrive sedan versions of the car in our market.
If you haven’t heard, the most affordable version starts at $49,900, and the xDrive all-wheel drive system is a $2,000 option. This model has a 2.0-liter TwinPower Turbo inline-six engine, which produces 255 horsepower (259 ps/190 kW) and 295 lb-ft (400 Nm) of torque. The 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) takes 5.9 seconds, regardless of whether we are talking about the rear-wheel drive or the all-wheel drive configuration.
As for the BMW M350 xDrive Sedan, it sits at the very top of the lineup, and will continue to do so until the next-generation M3 arrives. Rumor has it that the new M3 might launch in 2028, so that’s plenty of time for the new M350 to make a statement in the premium compact game for four-door rides. And chances are it will. After all, it is just as fast in a straight-line acceleration as the old base M3.
Photo: Instagram | ildar_project It takes just 4.1 seconds to hit 60 mph (97 kph) from a standstill, identical to the 2027 BMW M3 Sedan, which has 473 hp (480 ps/353 kW) to play with from its twin-turbo 3-liter inline-six. The M3 Competition and M3 Competition xDrive complete the sprint in 3.8 and 3.4 seconds, respectively, the spec sheet reveals.
BMW’s new M350 xDrive comes with 437 horsepower (443 ps/325 kW), and it features a twin-turbocharged 3.0-liter straight-six engine with 48-volt mild-hybrid assistance. The thrust is rated at 428 lb-ft (580 Nm), and pricing for this model kicks off at $65,900. Thus, it undercuts the base M3 by $13,400, as the latter kicks off at $79,300.
Just so you know, the new-gen 3 Series may indeed be new, but it builds on an updated version of the old model’s CLAR platform. And with this information off our chest, it is time to move on to the pictured car. Actually, make that the rendered car, because it came from @ildar_project on Instagram, and features a body kit that makes it stand out more.
This virtually-tuned 2027 BMW M350 xDrive features a new hood, has a sharp splitter attached to the factory bumper, special trim on the fenders, new side skirts, and what seem to be new door mirror casings, too. The rear diffuser with its two vertical brake lights is also new, and extends all the way to the rear wheels. There is also a ducktail spoiler that came from the aftermarket world, as well as what seems to be a carbon fiber trunk lid.
Photo: Instagram | ildar_project The car has a white paint finish on the outside, some glossy black elements for contrast, plenty of dry carbon details, and a set of Y-spoke alloys from Vossen. The wheels have a concave look, are much larger than the OEM ones, and fill the arches very nicely with the lowered ground clearance. By the way, those yellow daytime running lights are an OEM feature, not an aftermarket one, in case you forgot.
It is obvious that the body kit makes this new-gen BMW 3 Series stand out more, and for what it’s worth, it is on the appealing side of things, this writer thinks. Sure, not everyone may agree, as some would rather have the car bone stock, perhaps sprinkled with some factory M goodies from the options list, but this project is far from being a kitschy proposal. And we reckon it will be appreciated in certain circles.
Are you a fan of the design? And if you said yes, which I did, do you somehow like the Neue Klasse styling? That would obviously be a no for me, because the vizor-like face makes the new-gen BMW 3 Series (and not only) look confused, and some might easily mistake it for something that is a lot cheaper if it had no BMW roundles, especially on the outside.
The interior is not my cup of tea either, because it’s a screen fest that tries to keep the design quite minimalist, and chances are nobody will want the new-gen 3 Series used a few years from now, because it will probably be very much like an old smartphone. And nobody dreams about owning an old smartphone, right? Guess time will tell if I am right or wrong. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Ильдар (@ildar_project)

Mind Blown! Honda Does the Unthinkable and Drops an E-Bike at EICMA 2026 With a Carbon Y-Frame
21 photos
Photo: Cristian Curmei | Autoevolution
Heading off to EICMA, I expected to see the latest and freshest motorcycles, gear, and accessories. Little did I know that I would lock eyes with a unicorn. That unicorn is Honda’s RN0. Don’t go thinking about motorcycles, but rather, e-bikes.
Honda’s RN0 is a full-suspension e-MTB that has been completed in conjunction with none other than Rotwild, one of the most important collaborators that automotive giants shake hands with in order to bring their own spin to e-biking.
Rotwild has been present in the drive of brands such as Porsche, Mercedes- AMG , BMW, and a couple of others. They’ve often been called upon because most automotive brands don’t include production lines for e-bikes, and oddly enough, neither does Honda , even though they produce two-wheelers.
Photo: Cristian Curmei | Autoevolution At its core, the RN0 is built around a carbon fiber frame that runs as one piece, which Honda calls “exclusive,” mainly because it’s one of the only serious e-bikes these days that actually calls upon a frame style started off back in the 90’s. Brands like Cannondale and Trek ran with the design back then but some brands still produce bikes to this day around that very “Y.”
The folks that tested this RN0, in particular, Toni Bou, 40-time world champion rolling around on a Honda, and freeride MTB rider Antoine Buffart, utter the words “motorcross style” when it comes to the frame.
The rear suspension and the swingarm design (“Gullwing Swingarm”) are one that Honda mentions is from their own drawing books, and once a Fox Float X Factory rear shock is added to the mix, 145 mm of rear-wheel travel is accessed, so heading toward the downhill segment of MTBing, but not quite.
Photo: Cristian Curmei | Autoevolution At the front, a Fox 36 Factory fork is in place, ready with a whopping 160 mm of travel, Kashima coating on the stanchions, and a head tube angle that I found rather lax from my interactions with the RN0 at EICMA. Be sure to check out some of the images we caught from the show.
A dropped post is also integrated into the design, and oddly enough, hangs underneath the top arm of that “Y.” But it is important to note that the amount of travel you can access is dependency on frame size.
As for the drivetrain and the electronics responsible for giving this bike its kick, good old Shimano was called upon, granting access to a 750 W peak motor with 100 Nm (74 lb-ft) of torque. That's then coupled with auto shift function, auto assist, which analyzes rider input and delivers what’s asked for, and Trail+ mode, which makes changes to your assistance level, ranging from Eco to Boost, to always make you feel as though this one is letting it all loose, even though it isn’t; some scenarios simply require less power to get moving, others more.
Photo: Cristian Curmei | Autoevolution While it may seem new, and it surely is, the RN0 does build upon the RN01 that was designed for the 2003 World Cup circuit and seeing stardom in 2005 when Greg Minnaar won the UCI Downhill World Championship on the RN01.
Pricing is yet to be revealed so keep those eyes peeled for more Honda news from EICMA 2026.

One-Year Wonder: 1975 Plymouth Road Runner Marked the End of an Era
18 photos
Photo: brownie428/eBay
Introduced in 1968 as Plymouth's entry-level muscle car , the Road Runner soldiered on through 1975. Plymouth actually used the name until 1980, but only as a trim package on the compact Volare. The intermediate Road Runner was discontinued after the 1975 model year. It was the last iteration to use the B-body platform.
The latter is arguably the most important Mopar platform of the golden muscle car era. Introduced in 1962, it underpinned Chrysler's first mid-size vehicles, as well as the Dodges and Plymouths that got the iconic Max Wedge V8 engine. In the second half of the 1960s, the B-body platform spawned the iconic Satellite, GTX, Road Runner, Charger and Super Bee.
The Road Runner was among the most popular muscle cars in its early days. It moved 44,000 units in 1968 and over 81,000 examples in 1969. And while cars like the Super Bee and GTX were discontinued after Chrysler phased out its high-compression V8 engines in 1971, the Road Runner returned for a few more years.
1975 saw the arrival of the third-generation model . It was a more formal-looking B-body, this time around sharing much of its exterior design with the Plymouth Fury. The Road Runner was also available with a more upscale interior; with muscle cars long gone, most automakers tried to reposition their intermediates closer to the personal luxury car market.
Plymouth's attempt was rather unsuccessful. While the Fury moved over 110,000 examples, the Road Runner found just 7,183 customers. It was the nameplate's worst sales year and a notable decrease compared to both 1973 and 1974. For reference, the previous all-time low was 7,628 units in 1972.
But even though it's the rarest B-body Road Runner, the 1975 version is also the least desirable. And that's a shame, because I really like this body style. If you feel the same, then you have to check out this fine-looking coupe.
This Mopar emerged in Guttenberg, Iowa, and I have no idea whether it's an older restoration or a survivor . But I do know that it looks pretty good for a 51-year-old classic, with minor wear and tear, and still sporting an original V8 under the hood.
The only somewhat disappointing news about this Road Runner is that it doesn't have a big-block V8. The coupe rolled off the assembly line with the base 318-cubic-inch (5.2-liter) small-block V8. Plymouth also offered a 360-cubic-inch (5.9-liter) V8 and a 400-cubic-inch (6.6-liter) unit.
Records show that the entry-level mill found its way into 3,735 cars. If we also factor in the three-speed TorqueFlite automatic, this Road Runner is one of only 2,384 examples made with this drivetrain combo. It's not the rarest Mopar out there, but you won't see another one very soon.
If it's something you'd park in your driveway, this 1975 Road Runner is available for $19,500 . The owner is entertaining offers. How much is this Mopar worth?

One-of-6 Mopar: A Closer Look at the World's Most Expensive 1970 Road Runner Convertible
9 photos
Photo: CARFINDER/YouTube
About a week ago, I showed you a super-rare 1970 Plymouth Road Runner convertible that crossed the block for over $200,000 . Well, if you're a fan of factory pink Mopars, I have a full video walkaround of the car to show you.
The vehicle was shot while sitting on display before it went under the hammer in late October 2026. The Road Runner was auctioned off at Mecum's Dallas/Fort Worth 2026 auction, changing hands for $269,500. The sum included a 10% buyer's premium.
The sticker makes this Road Runner the third most expensive 1970 iteration ever sold at public auction. It's also the most expensive convertible of its kind, as well as the priciest 1970 Road Runner with a standard engine, regardless of the body style.
While the selling price is a bit surprising for a Mopar fitted with a 383-cubic-inch (6.3-liter) V8, it's not exactly shocking given the color. These factory pink Mopars have become increasingly more expensive in recent years, mainly because they're super rare .
Called Moulin Rouge on Plymouth cars and Panther Pink on Dodge models, FM3 is one of the 10 high-impact colors that Chrysler offered between 1969 and 1973. This hue is rare for quite a few reasons. For starters, pink was only available as a Spring Color in 1970. The option was on offer for only a couple of months.
Second, it was far from popular. Considered too feminine for a muscle car, it was ordered on only a tiny fraction of Mopars sold in 1970. Third, many of these vehicles were repainted in different colors by their second owners. Most people simply hated pink muscle cars back in the day.
This car is also rare due to the convertible top. Plymouth introduced a Road Runner drop top in 1969, selling just 1,890 units. Despite this low figure, the division kept the convertible in showrooms in 1970. Sales dropped even lower, with only 658 examples rolling off the assembly line.
Of these, three were ordered with the mighty 426-cubic-inch (7.0-liter) Hemi, while 34 were fitted with the 440-cubic-inch (7.2-liter) Six-Barrel V8. The remaining 621 units were delivered with the standard 383-cubic-inch powerplant. This Road Runner is also an automatic car, which makes it one of 429 built with this drivetrain combo.
How many of them were FM3 pink? Well, specific numbers are not available, but Mopar experts estimate that only 44 Road Runners were ordered in this hue in 1970. Only six of them were convertibles, and it's believed that just three are still around. Moreover, this example is said to be the only one with a matching-numbers drivetrain.
So, how come it's the most expensive 1970 convertible given that we have three more desirable Hemi units on the loose? Well, those have yet to go under the hammer at public events. They would probably fetch much more, but for that to happen, the owners would have to be willing to part ways with them. And it's unclear if all three are still around.
And interestingly enough, this pink Mopar fetched more than the priciest 1970 Road Runner with the rarer Six-Barrel V8. The previous record was set in 2025, when an unrestored V-code drop top changed hands at public auction for an impressive $220,000.
But that's enough history for today. Now hit the play button below for a full walkaround of this bright pink ragtop.

Save a Horse, Ride the Lingenfelter Mustang: 615+ RWHP, Vortech Blower, Price and Specs Coming Soon
30 photos
Photo: YouTube/Lingenfelter Performance Engineering
Check the thermostat in your garage right now, because hell has officially frozen over and it smells suspiciously like 93-octane gasoline and vaporized rear tires. Seeing the name Lingenfelter attached to a Ford Mustang feels like watching Darth Vader crash an Avengers barbecue wearing a Kiss the Cook apron and a Batman logo on his Starship Enterprise helmet. And yet, the multiverse unthinkable clash is official.
A seventh-generation S650 Ford Mustang GT gleaming in a wild white, blue, and black Stanadyne Performance livery with Lingenfelter upgrades feels like the automotive equivalent of swapping a Boss 429 with a 426 Hemi and calling it a Pontiac Super Duty.
As Carter MacEwen, the tuner’s marketing and media specialist, explained in the announcement YouTube video, the decision came down to pure mechanical respect. Ford and its 5.0-liter fourth-generation Coyote V8 offer a phenomenal foundation that generates massive horsepower with remarkable efficiency.
Wanting to try something fresh for Blue Oval enthusiasts, Lingenfelter teamed up with forced-induction specialist Vortech Superchargers to develop an in-house installed package right at its Wixom build facility.
Photo: YouTube/Lingenfelter Performance Engineering In bone-stock trim, the 2026 Mustang GT produces 480 hp (487 PS) and 415 lb-ft (563 Nm) of torque, or 486 hp (493 PS) and 418 lb-ft (567 Nm) with the active exhaust option. That is plenty for a grocery run, but Lingenfelter treats stock output as a polite acceptance to a “Hold my beer” challenge.
Unlike roots-type blowers that replace the intake manifold on top of the engine, this new Lingenfelter package utilizes a Vortech centrifugal supercharger mounted on the driver side of the engine bay. Breathing through a high-flow air filter, the gear-driven compressor pushes pressurized air through a massive front-mounted air-to-air intercooler tucked behind the lower grille before routing chilled boost upward through custom mandrel-bent aluminum charge pipes.
Cleverly, the upper charge tube splits into a Y-pipe with red silicone couplers that feed directly into both of the S650 Mustang GT's factory throttle bodies, retaining the original 5.0-liter intake manifold cover. Red Lingenfelter lettering sits atop the radiator shroud. Furthermore, the car's Stanadyne Performance wrap highlights Lingenfelter's ongoing partnership with the fuel-system giant known for high-flow injectors and direct-injection high-pressure fuel pumps.
Photo: YouTube/Lingenfelter Performance Engineering Once strapped to the rollers of the Dynojet Research chassis dynamometer, the Lingenfelterized blown Mustang unleashed a metallic shriek that could summon Henry Ford (both of them) and Zora Arkus-Duntov simultaneously. Running at 10 psi (0.69 bar) of boost pressure, the Coyote V8 laid down 607 hp (615 PS) at 7,460 rpm and 442 lb-ft (600 Nm) of torque at 7,010 rpm straight to the rear wheels during its validation pull.
Factoring in a typical 15 to 18 percent driveline loss, that rear-wheel readout translates to roughly 715 to 740 hp (725 to 750 PS) at the crankshaft, representing an increase of nearly 200 hp (203 PS) at the tires over a stock Mustang GT. On Michigan highways, the coupe celebrated by ripping ear-splitting pulls alongside a matching C8 Corvette, complementing the $9,995 Magnuson and Roush TVS2650 kit in Lingenfelter's catalog.
To understand why this announcement hits the muscle car community like a pyroclastic shockwave, look back at half a century of Detroit tribalism. Founded in 1973 in Decatur, Indiana, by the late NHRA drag racing icon John Lingenfelter, the company became the undisputed high temple of General Motors speed. Today, under owner Ken Lingenfelter, the firm operates out of Brighton and Wixom, Michigan, as royalty among Bowtie faithful.
Photo: YouTube/Lingenfelter Performance Engineering For over 50 years, if a vehicle wore a Chevrolet, Pontiac, Cadillac, Buick, or GMC badge, Lingenfelter turned it into an exotic-slaying weapon. The company built its legend on fourth-generation through eighth-generation Corvettes, including the 2001 twin-turbo 7.0-liter (427-cubic-inch) C5 that delivered 800 hp (811 PS) at the rear wheels and rocketed from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in a physics-defying 1.97 seconds during magazine testing.
Beyond Corvettes, the tuner dominated the street and strip with supercharged Camaros, Firebirds, Pontiac GTOs, Cadillac CTS-V and CT5-V Blackwing sedans, and even a 6.5-liter (396-cubic-inch) Chevrolet Tahoe that ran a 13.8-second quarter-mile at 96 mph (154 kph). However, with Chevrolet retiring the sixth-generation Camaro after 2024, Ford and its Mustang remained the last traditional American V8 pony car standing, prompting the Michigan engineers to cross party lines.
Photo: YouTube/Lingenfelter Performance Engineering While Carter MacEwen mentioned full pricing and specification sheets for the new Mustang packages are due in the coming months, the industry rumor mill is already spinning at redline. Unconfirmed rumors suggest that this SEMA-bound test mule is a rolling laboratory for a higher-boost Stage 2 package pairing Stanadyne's new RGX direct-injection fuel pump and injectors to push the Coyote past 850 hp (862 PS) on E85 fuel.
A second unconfirmed rumor whispers that Lingenfelter is preparing a serialized turnkey Mustang package featuring custom suspension hardware, active exhaust upgrades, and signature badging to rival traditional Ford tuners like Shelby, Saleen, and RTR. Even if Carter MacEwen admits it still feels weird to say “Lingenfelter Mustang” out loud, one fact is undeniable: when Bowtie royalty starts boosting Blue Oval legends, alterverses collide for a greater brotherhood of pistons.

Pennsylvania is putting $37 million in federal NEVI funding toward what PennDOT says will be 515 new public EV charging ports across the Philadelphia region, including curbside chargers.
The awards cover Bucks, Chester, Delaware, Montgomery, and Philadelphia counties. PennDOT says the projects will expand public charging availability by 27% across the region and 53% in Philadelphia.
Curbside charging gets a boost
For drivers without a driveway, curbside charging gives them somewhere to plug in while parked near home.
It’s Electric PA received $2.93 million for 157 on-street Level 2 ports across 13 Philadelphia neighborhoods. Voltpost received funding for another 62 curbside ports across the four suburban counties.

Fast charging is getting funding, too. PositivEnergy received $7.2 million for 54 DC fast-charging ports at 11 Philadelphia Parking Authority lots. Tesla received two $392,000 awards for eight ports each at Royal Farms in Broomall and Wawa in Plymouth Meeting.
NEVI moves into neighborhoods
The money comes from the federal National Electric Vehicle Infrastructure (NEVI) program, created by the Biden administration’s Bipartisan Infrastructure Law. Pennsylvania’s five-year allocation is $171.5 million.
NEVI initially focused on fast charging along designated highway corridors. States can spend the money more broadly after the Federal Highway Administration certifies that their corridor charging requirements have been met. Pennsylvania received that certification on September 22, 2025.
In fact, Pennsylvania has built 54 EV charging stations using NEVI funds so far – more than double the number of any other state.
PennDOT’s community charging program supports both Level 2 and DC fast charging. Its published program minimum requirements include at least four ports per proposed station, at least 6 kW per port, two ADA-compliant parking spaces, and J1772 or CCS connectors on every port. Equipment must also meet Buy America requirements.
More funding rounds are coming
PennDOT lists 71 awards in this southeastern round as part of its roughly $100 million statewide community charging effort.
Applications for the western region close November 20. Central and eastern Pennsylvania applications close March 12, 2027.
For the southeastern projects, PennDOT’s estimated schedule puts environmental reviews in November 2026 through January 2027, followed by agreement execution in January and February. Drivers will still have to wait for construction and commissioning before these awards become places to plug in.

BYD wasted no time, with sales of its new flagship electric sedan reaching 4,000 in just 19 days since its launch.
BYD Great Han EV sales surge after launch
With a record of more than 300,000 electric vehicles sold last month, BYD sold more EVs than the US did in the entire third quarter, combined.
A big part of the higher demand is thanks to BYD’s latest breakthrough technology, including its second-generation Blade Batteries and Flash Charging technology.
BYD began equipping vehicles with the new battery and charging tech in March, and over the past six months it has posted higher year-over-year sales growth. Through October, BYD sold 1,953,700 vehicles, up 6% compared to the same period in 2025.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
On October 13, BYD launched the Great Han, or “Da Han” in China, the first fully electric D-segment flagship sedan in its Dynasty lineup.
Just 19 days after its launch, BYD said Great Han EV sales reached 4,000 units. At that rate, sales could reach 10,000 or more in its first full month.
With “class-beating high value,” BYD said, “it has firmly established itself in the mid-to-high-end sedan segment above 250,000 yuan,” which is about $37,500.
The Great Han is available in three variants, priced from 235,900 yuan, or about $35,000. Buyers can choose from single- or dual-motor powertrains. The standard rear-wheel-drive (RWD) Premium trim offers up to 1,008 km (626 miles) of CLTC range, while the all-wheel-drive (AWD) Flagship variant offers up to 880 km (546 miles).
All models use a 102.326 kWh BYD Blade 2.0 battery pack. The RWD models have a single 370 kW (496 hp) motor, while the AWD variant adds a 200 kW (268 hp) front motor for a combined 570 kW (764 hp).
Like most of its new vehicles, the Great Han has a roof-mounted LiDAR and BYD’s God’s Eye B, a more advanced version of its intelligent driving system.
The ADAS system offers safety and convenience features, including Navigate on Autopilot on highways and in cities, plus remote autonomous parking.
All variants also include premium features, such as BYD’s DiSus-A dual-chamber air suspension system, rear-wheel steering, and zero-gravity front seats.
Measuring 5,256 mm in length, 1,999 mm in width, and 1,510 mm in height, with a 3,130 mm wheelbase, the Great Han is slightly bigger than the Tesla Model S and Lucid Air. It’s closer in size to the long-wheelbase Mercedes-Benz S-Class.
Thanks to BYD’s second-gen Blade Batteries and Flash Charging technology, the vehicle’s battery can charge from 10% to 70% in just 5 minutes. A full recharge (10% to 97%) takes just 9 minutes.
The Great Han joins the Great Tang SUV as the flagship sedan under BYD’s Dynasty lineup. BYD announced that Great Tang sales reached 14,000 units in October, marking four months of sales above 10,000.

Walmart has agreed to expand its commercial agreement with Symbiotic Inc. to automate an additional 25 U.S. regional distribution centers.
Symbiotic ( NASDAQ: SYM ) is an AI-powered warehouse automation and robotics company headquartered in Wilmington, Massachusetts.
Walmart ( NASDAQ: WMT ) will initially invest about $6 billion over several years to install high-tech equipment for moving cases at multiple locations, the companies said in a news release last week. Walmart has used Symbiotic products for a decade.
Why It Matters: Through the expansion, Walmart plans to bring additional automation capabilities to its regional distribution center network, supporting e-commerce upstream inventory management, increasing storage capacity and improving how products move through the supply chain. The capabilities will help Walmart offer customers a broader assortment, improve speed and provide more reliable replenishment across its network.
“At Walmart, we’re focused on bringing more items to more customers and members, faster than ever. Our investments in the physical and digital supply chain help us serve them however they choose to shop, whether in stores, at the curbside or at home,” said Rob Montgomery, executive vice president for Walmart U.S. Supply Chain Operations. “Our work with Symbotic over the years, including this expanded agreement, helps us improve service, grow capacity, simplify work for our associates and lower costs.”
Symbiotic produces several technologies, including high-density automated storage and retrieval systems, smart pallet-building systems and partial case fulfillment picking.
